writeup: TIC 313352561 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry data with an orbital period of 1.312182 days and a primary eclipse depth of 2.73%. The automated detection pipeline found the signal with very high confidence (signal-to-noise ratio of 213.1 in the periodogram analysis), and pixel-level imaging confirmed the eclipse signature near the target location with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 33.9. However, a data quality check revealed that eclipse depths alternate significantly between orbits - a pattern suggesting the actual period is double the initial automated measurement. No secondary eclipse was detected. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unknown candidate. While the strong detection significance and pixel-level confirmation suggest a genuine astrophysical source, the alternating eclipse-depth pattern indicates some complexity in the system that warrants further investigation.
